Her recent work examines how ponderosa pine and other Colorado Front Range forests regenerate after wildfire, how restoration treatments change understory plant diversity and invasion, and tools for post-fire reforestation. updates.name: Peter de Menocal
updates.bio: Marine geologist and paleoceanographer who became the eleventh president and director of Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution in October 2020. He uses deep-sea sediments to reconstruct past climate and ocean circulation. Earlier he held an endowed professorship at Columbia's Lamont-Doherty Earth Observatory, was Columbia's dean of science (2016-2019), and founded its Center for Climate and Life.

updates.bio: Senior scientist at NOAA's Global Monitoring Laboratory in Boulder. Trained at the University of Groningen (PhD 1978, tree-ring carbon isotopes), from 1985 until 2019 he ran NOAA's carbon cycle greenhouse gas group, building what became the Global Greenhouse Gas Reference Network, identified a large northern mid-latitude land CO2 sink, and invented the AirCore sampler (2002).

updates.name: Ralph F. Keeling
updates.bio: Geochemistry professor at UC San Diego's Scripps Institution of Oceanography (Geosciences Research Division). He pioneered precise interferometric measurement of atmospheric oxygen, now sampled at nine stations from the Arctic to Antarctica, and uses Ar/N2 ratios to track ocean heat storage. He also develops atmospheric methods for quantifying greenhouse gas emissions.
updates.research_interests: variations in atmospheric oxygen; recent perturbations to the global carbon cycle; air-sea gas exchange; detecting ocean heat storage and transport with atmospheric gases (Ar/N2); paleoclimate theory
